title: Transfer an electrode-roll mock by a spindle through its core
context: Core-based roll handling avoids gripping the wound material. This scaled inert task measures tool insertion and load support by a through-core spindle, ending with the roll suspended on bearing rests.
setup: Station table at z=747.5 mm; x forward, y left. Grey inert roll: 120 mm outer diameter, 50 mm width along y, 50 mm nominal bore, 150 g, low-infill 3D-printed polymer mock; starts axis y at (0.200,0.090), outer rim on the table. Two fixed rigid-polymer 10 x 40 x 25 mm chocks at x=0.144 and 0.256, y=0.090. Blue tubular aluminium spindle: outside diameter 18 mm, approximately 14.4 mm inside diameter, length 240 mm, 60 g tube plus two rigid polymer grip collars, total nominal 85 g. Each collar is 24 x 30 x 24 mm, centred 100 mm from the tube midpoint along either direction of y, rigidly fixed to the tube. The spindle starts axis y at (0.160,-0.160), resting flat on its collars on the table, axis height 12 mm. Fixed aluminium blue bearing pedestals: 60 x 18 x 116 mm at (0.320,+/-0.065); their top faces are 116 mm above the table. Each has two 6 x 18 x 25 mm cheeks centred x=0.305 and 0.335, leaving a 24 mm opening. Only these objects and the standard rig are present. All dimensions are scaled benchmark choices, not production roll specifications.
scoring: Primary final score 0-1. At every 20 Hz control sample, both TCPs must remain >=30 mm outside the oriented 120 x 50 x 120 mm roll bounding box; any violation gives sticky zero until reset. Every score tier also requires both TCPs >=30 mm outside both movable bounding boxes and both objects still (<5 mm/s, <0.1 rad/s). Zero for invalid poses or an object >5 mm below table. Threaded: spindle axis within 3 degrees of roll axis; finite spindle passes both bore faces with >=25 mm protrusion, and the projected tube and every collar section inside the bore slab fit all 24 bore half-planes (0.8 mm numerical allowance). Threaded scores 0.25. Threaded with roll centre within 3 mm in x and 6 mm in y of (0.320,0), axis within 3 degrees of y, scores 0.5. Score 1 additionally requires spindle spanning both rest top faces, bottom within 1.5 mm of their tops, line x within 2 mm at both rests, centre y within 5 mm of zero, axis within 2 degrees of y, and roll hanging below spindle by 15.79 +/-2 mm with its underside >=40 mm above the table. Otherwise highest satisfied tier applies; success holds 1 s. The TCP exclusion is a conservative handling rule, not a measurement of all robot surface contacts. Physical scoring uses front/top photos, ruler, bore/spindle sizes and the full video to check the handling envelope.
fidelity: Rigid roll with 24 convex sector colliders leaves the bore open; the spindle is a cylinder plus two rigid grip collars. Native contacts carry the load; no attachments or teleports. Geometry, inertia and friction are scaled approximations. No web flexibility, tension, coating damage, dust, solvents or electrochemistry. The 20 Hz TCP exclusion is a conservative proxy; it cannot detect every link contact or events between samples. Original MIT USD generators are included.
reset_notes: Put the roll back between the chocks and the spindle on its mark. Clear handling history by resetting the episode. No materials are consumed.
instruction: Insert the blue spindle through the electrode roll's hollow core, lift the spindle by its ends, and set it across both blue bearing rests so the roll hangs centered midway between them. Keep both gripper TCPs at least 30 mm outside the roll's bounding box throughout; do not handle the roll directly. Release the spindle and move both grippers at least 30 mm clear of both movable objects.
scores: Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta): 0.0; scripted physics demo: 1.0. Both seed 0; model 2400 steps (120 s), demo 1093 steps (54.65 s) with a completed 1 s success hold.
